## 🔴 Errors (likely to cause subtle bugs or inconsistent behavior)

### 🔴 E1 — Package version drift: `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions`

| Project | Version |
|---|---|
| Core | 8.0.0 |
| Services | **8.0.1** |
| Api | 8.0.0 |

Services references 8.0.1 while Core and Api reference 8.0.0. Because NuGet resolves to the *highest requested version* at build time, the runtime will use 8.0.1 anyway — but the intent is unclear, and a developer updating one project may not know to update the others. This is a classic version-drift symptom that Central Package Management (CPM) eliminates entirely.

### 🔴 E2 — Package version drift: test infrastructure packages

| Package | Api.Tests | Core.Tests |
|---|---|---|
| Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk | **17.9.0** | **17.10.0** |
| xunit | **2.7.1** | **2.8.1** |
| xunit.runner.visualstudio | **2.5.6** | **2.8.1** |
| NSubstitute | 5.1.0 | 5.1.0 |

Two test projects using different test-framework versions means tests may pass in one project and fail in another due to behavioral differences between xunit 2.7 and 2.8 (e.g., changed default parallelization, new assertion semantics). This is a real correctness risk.

---

## 🟡 Warnings (anti-patterns that should be fixed)

### 🟡 W1 — No `Directory.Build.props` — 7 properties duplicated across all 5 projects

Every single project file repeats this identical block:

```xml
<TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
<Nullable>enable</Nullable>
<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
<EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
<Company>Contoso</Company>
<Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
```

This violates the DRY principle. When you need to update to `net9.0`, you must edit 5 files instead of 1. Any single omission creates a silent configuration mismatch.

**Fix:** Create `Directory.Build.props` at the repo root:

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
    <EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
    <Company>Contoso</Company>
    <Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!-- Test project defaults -->
  <PropertyGroup Condition="$(MSBuildProjectName.EndsWith('.Tests'))">
    <IsPackable>false</IsPackable>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

Then strip all 7 properties (+ `IsPackable`) from every `.csproj`.

### 🟡 W2 — No Central Package Management — scattered, inconsistent versions

All package versions are specified inline in each `.csproj` with no single source of truth. This is the direct cause of the version drift in E1 and E2.

**Fix:** Create `Directory.Packages.props` at the repo root:

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- Production packages -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions" Version="8.0.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Swashbuckle.AspNetCore" Version="6.5.0" />
    <PackageVersion Include="System.Text.Json" Version="8.0.5" />

    <!-- Test packages -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk" Version="17.10.0" />
    <PackageVersion Include="xunit" Version="2.8.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" Version="2.8.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="NSubstitute" Version="5.1.0" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

Then remove `Version="..."` from every `<PackageReference>` in all `.csproj` files, leaving just:

```xml
<PackageReference Include="xunit" />
```

### 🟡 W3 — `DocumentationFile` duplicated across 3 src projects

All three source projects contain the identical property:

```xml
<DocumentationFile>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
```

This should be centralized. Since test projects typically don't need XML docs, scope it to non-test projects.

**Fix:** Add to `Directory.Build.props`:

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="!$(MSBuildProjectName.EndsWith('.Tests'))">
  <DocumentationFile>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

Then remove `<DocumentationFile>` from all 3 src `.csproj` files.

### 🟡 W4 — `PrintBuildInfo` target copy-pasted across 3 src projects

This identical custom target appears in Core, Services, and Api:

```xml
<Target Name="PrintBuildInfo" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Message Importance="high" Text="Building $(AssemblyName) [$(Configuration)]" />
</Target>
```

Duplicated targets are a maintenance hazard — if you want to add timing info or change the format, you must edit 3 files.

**Fix:** Create `Directory.Build.targets` at the repo root:

```xml
<Project>
  <Target Name="PrintBuildInfo" BeforeTargets="Build"
          Condition="!$(MSBuildProjectName.EndsWith('.Tests'))">
    <Message Importance="high" Text="Building $(AssemblyName) [$(Configuration)]" />
  </Target>
</Project>
```

Then remove the `<Target>` block from all 3 src `.csproj` files.

Core, Services, and Api each have two separate `<PropertyGroup>` elements — the main one and a second one for just `DocumentationFile`. These should be merged into a single block for readability (or better yet, centralized per W3).

### 🔵 S1 — Consider adding `GenerateDocumentationFile` instead of `DocumentationFile`

The modern SDK-style approach is:

```xml
<GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>

This automatically sets `DocumentationFile` to the conventional path. It's more idiomatic and less error-prone than manually constructing the path with `$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml`.

### 🔵 S2 — Test projects: consider adding `coverlet.collector` for code coverage

Neither test project includes a coverage collector. If code coverage is desired (common in CI), add:

```xml
<PackageVersion Include="coverlet.collector" Version="6.0.2" />
```

The `.sln` file uses `{FAE04EC0-301F-11D3-BF4B-00C04F79EFBC}` (legacy C# project GUID) for all projects including the Web SDK project.
